title: Admission Moderator: resilience for quota controller outages, burst pacing and multi-region failover
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem statement: Recent incidents show our central quota controller can become a single point of pain during regional network partitions and flash bursts. When the limiter fabric loses the lease or RPCs stall, customers observe long tail latencies, opaque 429 spikes, and cascading retries that violate token-level SLOs. This ticket designs and implements an Admission Moderator layer that: 1) provides degraded but fair admission when quota store is partially unavailable, 2) enforces burst pacing to avoid downstream stalls, 3) integrates with multi-region circuit-breakers and prioritized shedding policies, and 4) emits telemetry needed for SLO guardrails and automated rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Admission Moderator runs alongside existing limiter without schema changes and can be toggled via console feature flag
During upstream quota store outage, Admission Moderator allows controlled admissions for P0/P1 traffic with proportional fairness and rejects lower-priority requests deterministically
End-to-end median+P99 request latency for admitted requests remains within current SLOs under simulated outage and synthetic burst workloads
New telemetry: per-tenant admitted_rate, denied_rate, pacing_delay_ms, and heuristic_fallback_reason visible in console with 7d retention
Runbook updated and chaos-playbook verified in staging: simulated RPC stalls, region isolation, and spike tests pass without cascading failures

2026-02-22 - Use priority tiers (P0,P1,P2) with configurable weight vectors per tenant rather than per-route weights to simplify rollout (PM feedback: Jonah)

implementation_notes: Admission Moderator components: local soft-credit reservoir, fast estimator for recent request rate, pacing queue with token-less admission window, and probabilistic backoff generator
Local soft-credits are replenished from the quota store when RPCs succeed; on failure, slow decay algorithm reduces credits gracefully instead of immediate drain
Fairness policy: weighted round-robin across tenant priority classes with alpha smoothing to prevent starvation during bursts
Pacing algorithm: adaptive initial delay = min(50ms, 0.1 * observed_interarrival_ms) with exponential backoff under repeated denials
Circuit integration: link to circuit state machine in infra repo and subscribe to health events via event bus; Admission Moderator honors circuit OPEN state immediately
Rollback: feature flag + kill-switch exposing immediate pass-through (temporary open) plus automated telemetry-based revert if SLO degradation detected

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: probabilistic admission could cause higher variance for small tenants. Mitigation: floor guarantees for small tenants and synthetic slow-start ramp for first 60s

Risk: added latency from pacing queue might push some routes over SLO. Mitigation: aggressive canary with auto-revert; monitor pacing_delay_ms histogram and p99 latency; immediate pass-through flag if breach detected
Risk: misconfigured weights lead to starvation. Mitigation: conservative default weights, validation at config-time, and telemetry-based alerts when admitted_rate_ratio deviates >25% from expected
Risk: complexity increases operational burden. Mitigation: runbook, metrics, and single-command kill-switch; training session for oncall
qa_plan: Unit and integration tests for local reservoir, pacing queue, and weight scheduler
Staging chaos tests: quota-store RPC drop, region network partitions, steady-state high-QPS bursts, and tenant mix skewed towards low-latency-sensitive customers
Loadbench: 1hr soak at 20k qps with realistic tenant distribution; validate P50/P99 latency and error budget consumption
Customer-facing QA: small set of internal tenants and two pilot customers (opt-in) for early feedback
rollout_plan: Stage 0: feature flag off in prod; merged behind FF
Stage 1: enable for infra-only tenants in us-west-2 (5%) - 48h observation
Stage 2: enable for 25% of tenants across two regions - 72h observation
Stage 3: gradual ramp to 100% with staggered regional enablement and SLO guardrails enforced
Rollback: immediate disable via FF or cluster-level pass-through; automated alert if SLO breach detected

notes: This ticket complements recent quota-store replication work (ENG-412345). The hybrid local-soft-credit approach favors eventual consistency and graceful degradation over strict global correctness.
We intentionally avoid copying full token buckets cross-region due to replication cost; instead rely on probabilistic admission + telemetry to achieve fairness goals.
If canary shows unexpected SLO regressions, we will pause and revert feature flag, and run targeted postmortem with simulated inputs used during the failure window.
